paragraphs: I'm applying for the Ridership Analysis and Modeling internship in the MTA's Spring Emerging Talent program. I'm an MBA (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli in New York, and before school I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. I ride the subway every day, and the idea of working on the numbers behind how NYC Transit plans service is a big part of why this role stands out to me.

At Lenovo I built forecasts, models and scenario analyses to evaluate capital allocation, which improved capital efficiency by 15%, and I ran variance, sensitivity and trend analyses that I turned into recommendations for cross-functional teams. At JPMorgan Asset Management I built analytics frameworks to track KPIs across platforms and synthesized large datasets into dashboards and reporting for senior leadership.

Ridership work looks like the same core job: clean the data, find the trend, build a model and explain it plainly to the people making decisions. I'm comfortable in Excel, Tableau and Python, and I can commit the weekly hours the program asks for. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
